title: 5. Leading Operational KPIs, Structural Potential & CEO Walk-the-Talk
summary_box: Six leading KPIs govern post-demerger INDIAGLYCO. These include continuing BSPC quarterly revenue of ₹357–362 Cr in H1 FY27 and operating margin recovery above 11%. Analysts must also track Clariant IGL JV profits, dividend upstreaming, and net borrowings halved to ₹826 Cr. Inventory days and the ethanol-to-crude-MEG spread complete the dashboard. Over FY22–FY26, CEO Rupark Sarswat and CFO Anand Singhal cut debt, cleared promoter pledges, shifted BSPC mix, and completed the demerger. However, Ennature's export margins lagged prior expectations.

epigraph.quote: Management credibility is not measured by the eloquence of the five-year vision, but by whether the balance sheet looks like the promise five years later.
epigraph.author: Institutional Stewardship Principle

web_blocks.html: The September 2026 demerger reset INDIAGLYCO's accounting perimeter. Tracking historical consolidated totals without separating continuing KPIs will mislead any analyst. We must evaluate whether the retained BSPC + Industrial Gases + 49% Clariant JV business is compounding or stalling. Six leading operational KPIs matter most for this assessment [1][6][7][10].

web_blocks.caption: Six Leading Operational KPIs for Post-Demerger INDIAGLYCO
rows: 1. Continuing BSPC + Gases Quarterly Revenue
Steady sequential growth toward ₹380–420 Cr/qtr
PASS_WITH_WATCH: Sequential uptick (+1.5% QoQ) after exiting low-margin traded goods [6].
2. Continuing Operating Margin (OPM %)
11.0% in Q1 FY27 & Q2 FY27 [1]
Recovery toward 13%–15% via glycol ethers mix
WATCH: Down from 14%–17% pre-demerger (which included ~21% EBIT spirits) [1][9].
3. Net Borrowings & Quarterly Interest
Borrowings ₹826 Cr (Sep 2026); Interest ₹12 Cr/qtr [1]
Interest <15% of EBITDA; Net Debt/EBITDA <2.0x

WATCH: ₹48 Cr annualized interest is 30.8% of ₹156 Cr standalone continuing EBITDA (above <15% threshold) and ₹826 Cr gross debt is 5.29x standalone EBITDA, though halved vs. Mar 2026 (₹1,691 Cr) [1].
4. Clariant IGL JV (49% Stake) PAT & Dividends
49% PAT share + multi-crore interim dividends [10][11]
Rising Bio-EO offtake & consistent JV PAT growth
PASS: Core margin-accretive anchor supporting consolidated PAT [10][11].
5. Inventory Days & Cash Conversion Cycle
139 Inventory Days; 47-day CCC (FY26) [1]
Inventory <140 days; negative/low WC days
PASS: Sharply improved from 224 inventory days in FY24 [1].
6. Bio-Feedstock vs. Crude-MEG Spread
Grain/molasses cost volatility vs. global MEG [6][17]
Specialty glycol ethers > commodity MEG share
WATCH: Structural sensitivity to Indian cane/grain prices and crude oil [6][17].
web_blocks.takeaway: Balance-sheet and working-capital KPIs have inflected positively; the primary operational watchpoint is lifting standalone BSPC OPM from 11% toward 13%–15%.

web_blocks.html: 3–5 Year CEO & CFO Walk-the-Talk Audit (FY22–FY27): Chief Executive Officer Rupark Sarswat and Chief Financial Officer Anand Singhal led a complex multi-year restructuring [6][12]. They steered India Glycols through major structural changes in Indian mid-cap chemicals. Their record from FY22 through Q2 FY27 shows high execution discipline on capital structure and corporate simplification. Management also candidly acknowledged export headwinds in the now-demerged biopharma unit [6][15][16].

web_blocks.takeaway: Management delivered on every major structural, balance-sheet, and demerger commitment over FY22–FY26, earning high marks for capital-allocation follow-through.

web_blocks.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
paragraphs: In Indian mid-cap industrials, few teams dismantle an 80%+ share-pledge overhang while bringing in a Swiss multinational JV partner. Fewer still raise ₹467 Cr of equity alongside promoters and hand shareholders direct 1:1 and 1:3 shares in two growth verticals.

That track record earns management the benefit of the doubt on intent. Still, KPI health remains PASS_WITH_WATCH rather than an unqualified PASS. An 11% standalone OPM leaves a thin buffer if feedstock inflation spikes.

book_paragraphs: When you evaluate a management team over a five-year arc, ignore the adjectives in their press releases and line up their old promises next to the audited balance sheet. Five years ago, India Glycols carried heavy debt, a history of promoter share pledges, and a sprawling conglomerate structure that confused chemical analysts and liquor investors alike.

Look at what CEO Rupark Sarswat and CFO Anand Singhal actually did between 2021 and late 2026. First, they closed the Clariant joint venture and used the proceeds to retire expensive NBFC debt. Second, when Red Sea shipping disruptions and cheap Chinese chemical exports hit BSPC, Sarswat refused to chase empty top-line numbers—he deliberately walked away from low-margin traded chemical contracts to defend core plant margins.

Third, in November 2025, the promoter group put cash on the table alongside institutional investors in a ₹466.99 Cr preferential allotment, driving promoter share pledges down to zero. Fourth, they shepherded the three-way demerger through the NCLT Allahabad Bench without a single derailment, making it effective on September 1, 2026.

Were there misses? Yes—Ennature Biopharma's export margins stayed under pressure from Turkish and Western competition, never quite breaking out before it was spun into its own listed vehicle. And now, for the remaining India Glycols Limited, you and I have six clear dashboard dials to watch every quarter: continuing BSPC revenue above ₹360 Cr, operating margins climbing back from 11% toward 13%–15%, interest staying near ₹12 Cr a quarter, steady Clariant JV profit and dividend upstreaming, tight inventory days, and the spread between Indian bio-feedstocks and global crude-linked MEG.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
paragraphs: Walk-the-talk discipline reduces governance risk dramatically, but it cannot repeal commodity math. In Chapter 6, we open the full 10-year Screener ledger to examine how ROE, debt, and cash conversion really behaved beneath the surface.
